title: Buddy Petit, Kid Rene, Chris Kelly and Papa Celestin
summary: He praises Petit's execution, Rene's round tone, Kelly's blues, and Celestin's sweet style, and says he joined Celestin's band shortly before his death.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Did you hear Buddy Petit much?
Oh, I played with Buddy.
Piano.

Yeah, I played piano with Buddy. Buddy was one of the finest trumpet players. Now, he wasn't strong and powerful, but I mean, he had so much execution. I mean, to my, Buddy, Buddy had the time at the execution that they're using today. I think he's just that far ahead of time. I'd say, I'd put about 40 years ahead of time.
In what ways was his execution good?
In diminishing and chords. Diminishing. That's what they're using today. That's what Buddy made 40 years ago.
Did he play high like Armstrong does?
No, he couldn't play high. That was only his trouble. He never did believe in playing high. He'd stay in the staff and make you sick, though. Make you dizzy with the variation he'd make.
Could you hum a typical variation? Do you remember any of them?
Well, I tell you, he used to play so many variations. He used to practically make a whole lot of different. The immediate execution, under control.
Fingering was good.
Fingering, yeah.
Used carnet or trumpet the times you heard him?
Well, the time I heard him, he had a B-flat trumpet. He was a very fine trumpet player.
What about Kid Rene? How did he compare?

He was a trumpet player on a different type. He had a swell, round tone and clean, clean, clean. I mean, him and Louis Armstrong were about the only two I know on that tone type. It's just a tone. I mean, I heard a lot of trumpet players. I mean, they imitate you, you know, close. A shocker. A shocker played more like Rene than anybody I heard yet. He's styling everything.
Is Rene pretty loud or soft?

Yeah, he was loud. He could get out there on the back of the truck doing the advertising days and get on the back on the tailgate of the truck and stand up there. When he hit, he'd see, this is Claire.
I see.
I see, yeah. This is Claire.
What about Chris Kelly?
Well, Chris Kelly, he was more of a blues trumpet player. In fact, he was one of the best blues trumpets to play their head around here.
What about Papa Celestan? Did he rank with the very best in those days? Was he one of the great players?

Well, yeah, Papa did. He shared. But Papa, I mean, was a different type, too. I mean, that's another type of trumpet. Papa was more of a sweet, sweet type. He had numbers he featured, like Josephine, whenever you launch some telephone to me, well, I mean, he used to specialize.
When did you first play with Papa?
Well, I played a lot of jobs off and on with Papa, you know, but I wasn't regular. I got in a band about five months before Papa died. I was appointed, you know.
I think that about covers most of everything. We only got about two seconds left on here. Okay. Let that run once here.
